newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain offshore banking units assets edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain offshore banking units assets edge higher.

text.p: Total assets of offshore banking units (OBUs) operating in Bahrain rose slightly at end-September to $67.116 billion compared with $67.098 billion a year earlier, Bahrain Monetary Agency (BMA) figures showed on Sunday.
The end-September figure was also higher than the $61.498 billion reported at end-June 1996.
The BMA, Bahrain's central bank, did not say how many OBUs were operating on the island, but it said earlier there were 48 OBUs at the end of 1995.
There were 75 units in Bahrain at the start of the oil boom in the mid-1970s. Their assets peaked at $72.58 billion in 1989.
The assets of 19 commercial banks fell to 2.53 billion dinars ($6.71 billion) at end-September 1996 from 2.64 billion dinars a year earlier and 2.57 billion dinars at end-June 1996.
Bahrain is the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
